headline: Massachusetts seeks answers after ICE arrests on South Coast
dek: Gov. Maura Healey's office says at least a dozen people were arrested in New Bedford as advocates documented dozens more detentions across nearby communities.
body: Massachusetts officials are seeking information from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after a multi-day enforcement operation began on the South Coast last week, with arrests reported in New Bedford and nearby communities.

Gov. Maura Healey's office said it received reports that ICE arrested at least a dozen people in New Bedford on Sept. 21. WBUR reported that advocates had documented 34 arrests by Sept. 24, while GBH News reported advocates said at least 40 people had been detained in New Bedford, along with additional arrests in Fall River. Those figures came from advocates and were not confirmed by ICE.

Regional reporting described agents making arrests near workplaces, grocery stores, gas stations and public streets. Lawyers and immigrant-support organizations worked to locate detainees and file habeas petitions, with some people held at ICE facilities in Massachusetts and Rhode Island, according to WBUR and GBH News.

Healey said many families were left without information about where relatives were being held or why they had been arrested. New Bedford Mayor Jon Mitchell also criticized the operation and said city officials had not received a response from ICE about its scope, WBUR reported.

ICE confirmed enforcement activity in Massachusetts but declined to provide details about the New Bedford operation. The agency gave WBUR a list of five convicted people arrested in Massachusetts, though the outlet said those cases did not appear connected to the South Coast arrests. The governor's office and local advocates continue to press for information about the detainees and access to legal assistance.
location: New Bedford and the South Coast, Massachusetts
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Massachusetts Seeks Answers After ICE Arrests in New Bedford
seoDescription: Massachusetts officials are seeking information after ICE made arrests in New Bedford and nearby South Coast communities.
